thread:
tess: Heads up — APAC midnight product launch looks like a concentrated 2.5h spike (SEA + JP). Projections show ~3x baseline QPS, heavy tail on long-chat prompts. We need a concrete GPU-hour forecast + cost hedge plan. :eyes:
raj: Numbers pls — peak QPS, expected token volume, and what mix of reserved/spot we want.
tess: Quick sketch: estimated total extra tokens ~45M over 2.5h -> rough steady-state additional throughput ~5.0k tokens/s peak. With our current latency targets and 2k token sequences average, that maps to ~12k GPU-hours on A100 if we serve full fp16. If we push q4_0 quantized model for non-critical flows we can lower to ~6.8k GPU-hours.
anna: re: networking — SEA AZs have limited cross-AZ NIC headroom; avoid large cross-zone KV prefill traffic during ramp. Plan prewarm locally per-AZ.
raj: Cost delta ballpark?
tess: Back-of-envelope: reserved A100-style pool cost for the window (if buying committed hours) ~= $3.2/hr * 12k = $38.4k. Spot mix (70% spot / 30% reserved) reduces to ~ $18k but risk of reclaim + rollout complexity. If we use quantized baseline for 40% of traffic AND use cheaper L4s for short requests, we can hit ~ $14k. These are rough — need pricing from finance. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
samir: For resilience, propose 3-tier routing: primary (APAC local dedicated), overflow (APAC spot pool), fallback (EU warm pool with 30-50ms added latency). Also knob: route low-SLA or auxiliary functions to smaller quantized variants.
tess: Concrete ops plan:
- Prewarm: spin warm-pool 45m before launch, warm 20% KV cache with top-50 prompt prefixes. Do per-AZ prefill only.
- Autoscale: shorter ramp (10-20m) with aggressive initial burst allowance. Suggested autoscale config:
```
min_replicas: 40
initial_burst_replicas: 120
max_replicas: 220
scale_up_window_minutes: 15
kv_prefill_pct: 20
```
- Model mix: 60% fp16 (reserved), 30% q4_0 (spot), 10% tiny-quant fallback (cpu if needed).
- Fallbacks: if spot reclaim > 5% in a region, route 25% traffic to EU warm-pool and enable degraded-latency mode.

raj: Are we confident 20% KV prefill is enough? cold KV hits are expensive.
tess: We profiled last Q launch — prefill 20% reduced 95th latency by ~120ms and saved ~18% GPU-hours because KV misses cause more decoding. For this workload I recommend 20-30%.
anna: Ops caveat: cross-AZ prefill will saturate our pod egress in ap-southeast-1 at ~700MB/s if we prefill >30%. Keep it AZ-local.
samir: Also need to update network egress allowances for warm-pool boot (NAT gateway quota). I'll open a quick ticket with infra NAT team.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: tomorrow 23:10 PT -> will run 15-min steady-state test at 50% traffic to quantized path, alert if 95th latency > 800ms.
raj: Action items:
- raj: verify reserved hour purchase / finance approval for emergency buffer (target: 5k reserved GPU-hours).
- anna: run per-AZ prewarm script and validate egress metrics + KV warm-up (use subset list).
- tess: update launch runbook with autoscale parameters, routing rules, and fallback thresholds.
- samir: open NAT/egress ticket and prepare EU warm-pool cold start checklist.

tess: I'll also attach a small prewarm curl for the runbook — use only in pre-launch window: 
```
# prefill top-50 prefixes into KV cache
for p in top50.txt; do
  curl -X POST https://inference.redwood/api/v1/serve/prefill \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $LAUNCH_TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-large-q4_0","prefix": "'$p'"}' &
done
```

anna: A few more checks: ensure instance sharding preserves KV locality, and throttle prefill to 200 concurrent requests per AZ.
raj: Good. I'll sync with finance and confirm reserved purchase by EOD. If we get approval, we lock 5k reserved hours and keep a 30% spot buffer.
tess: Thanks — I'll post the updated runbook and a short checklist in #eng-infra an hour after finance confirms. :thumbsup:
